children.label: a
children.prompt: Write the coordinates of the point of intersection of lines B and C and hence give the solution to the simultaneous equations for these lines.

teachingMapping.rationale: Classification of revised source content; no teaching-content edits.

answer.worked: Lines B and C intersect at $(2, 2)$, so the simultaneous solution is $x = 2, y = 2$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the graph to solve the equations for lines A and C simultaneously (give an estimate).

teachingMapping.rationale: Classification of revised source content; no teaching-content edits.

answer.worked: Lines A and C intersect at approximately $(0.4, 2.8)$, so $x \approx 0.4, y \approx 2.8$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Can the equations for lines A and B be solved simultaneously? Explain why or why not.

teachingMapping.rationale: Classification of revised source content; no teaching-content edits.

answer.worked: No, they are parallel so will never meet. There’s no pair of $x$ and $y$ values that will solve both equations.
